les: Van 'n kamer vol masjien tot kabels onder die see
kaps_punt: Verandering in die moderne vorms van kommunikasie: Rekenaar; Internet

items.bewering: 'n Selfoon is 'n rekenaar, en die masjien op 'n lessenaar is ook een.
items.blok: Rekenaars wat 'n hele kamer gevul het
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary, 'handheld' (a small electronic device or computer that fits in the hand); smartphone defined in reference and legal glossaries as a cell phone combined with a handheld computer that runs applications. Holds for a modern (slim)foon, which is what a Grade 4 learner will picture.

items.bewering: Die eerste rekenaars het baie anders as albei gelyk. Een rekenaar het 'n hele kamer van die een muur tot die ander gevul.
items.blok: Rekenaars wat 'n hele kamer gevul het
items.bron: Smithsonian Magazine, 'The brief history of the ENIAC computer' (U-shaped machine filling a room of about 1 500 sq ft); ENIAC's 40 panels stood along three walls of the room (ENIAC reference entries, Computer Hope). The superlative is safe as worded: it says the first computers looked very different from a phone and a desktop, which holds even for the desk-sized Atanasoff-Berry Computer (Computer History Museum catalogue 102781093: about the size of a large desk, 750 lb), and it attributes the room-filling only to 'een rekenaar', not to all of them.

items.bewering: Universiteite, regerings en groot besighede het sulke masjiene gehad, nie mense by die huis nie.
items.blok: Rekenaars wat 'n hele kamer gevul het
items.bron: Computer History Museum timeline: first UNIVAC I delivered to the US Census Bureau, 1951; 46 million-dollar UNIVAC systems installed in six years. Centre for Computing History / LEO Computers Society: LEO, built by J. Lyons & Co, the first business data-processing computer. ENIAC was built at the University of Pennsylvania for the US Army; the ABC at Iowa State (Iowa State University digital collections).

items.bewering: 'n Mens moes eers leer hoe om so 'n masjien te gebruik.
items.blok: Rekenaars wat 'n hele kamer gevul het
items.bron: Columbia University Computing History, ENIAC page (programs set up by plugging cables into about 40 plugboards, taking days per problem); accounts of the ENIAC programmers (Longreads 2014, after Isaacson) who had to learn the machine from its wiring diagrams.

items.bewering: Met die jare het die dele binne 'n rekenaar al hoe kleiner geword. Die masjien wat 'n kamer gevul het, kon toe op een lessenaar staan. Rekenaars het ook vinniger geword en meer werk in 'n dag gedoen.
items.blok: Hoe rekenaars kleiner en makliker geword het
items.bron: Computer History Museum, 'The Silicon Engine' (transistor, then integrated circuits and microprocessors; IC circuits 'orders of magnitude smaller, faster, and less expensive' than discrete components). 'Die masjien ... kon toe op een lessenaar staan' is read as the same computing capability fitting on a desk, which holds for desktop machines from the late 1970s onward.

items.bewering: Hulle het makliker geword om te gebruik met knoppies en prente op 'n skerm. Nou kan 'n kind by die huis self een gebruik.
items.blok: Hoe rekenaars kleiner en makliker geword het
items.bron: Smithsonian Insider and The Henry Ford on the graphical user interface (Xerox PARC 1970s, Apple Macintosh 1984): users clicked icons, pictures representing programs, instead of typing commands, making computers usable by non-specialists.

items.bewering: Waarvoor ons rekenaars vandag gebruik: boodskappe oor 'n lang afstand stuur; skoolwerk en navorsing; dokumente tik en stoor; planne ontwerp, kuns en musiek maak; 'n bank se geld en 'n besigheid se werk bestuur; hospitale, banke en winkels werk elke dag hiermee; skole en laboratoriums bewaar hulle inligting op rekenaars.
items.bron: General descriptive uses, consistent with the computer definition and the business/government use history above (CHM, LEO Computers Society); no item claims exclusivity or a date. Checked as a set: none of the seven items overstates what a computer does.

items.bewering: Een rekenaar alleen kan net by sy eie inligting uitkom.
items.bron: Follows from the definition of a network as connected computers sharing information (Cornell, 'The Internet and the World Wide Web', ch. 2; RIT networking notes): an unconnected computer has only the data stored on or loaded into it.

items.bewering: Die internet is die stelsel wat rekenaars oor die hele wêreld aan mekaar koppel. Ons noem dit 'n wêreldwye netwerk van rekenaars wat inligting met mekaar deel.
items.bron: Internet Society, 'Brief History of the Internet' (Leiner, Cerf, Kahn et al.); Cornell DigLib ch. 2 and the 1987 TCP/IP primer describing the internet as interconnected networks of computers worldwide.

items.bewering: Nuus en foto's loop deur hierdie netwerk van land tot land. Die meeste daarvan reis as lig deur kabels op die seebodem.
items.bron: TeleGeography Submarine Cable FAQ (data travels as light: lasers send pulses through thin glass fibres; cables rest on the seabed in deep water and are buried beneath it near shore); TeleGeography 2023 Mythbusting part 3 (over 99% of intercontinental data traffic on submarine cables; satellites about 0.37% of US international capacity); ITU as cited in the Financial Express (over 99% of international data traffic). 'Die meeste' is a safe quantifier even allowing for overland routes between neighbouring countries.

items.bewering: Net soos die kabels van die telegraaf loop hulle onder die see deur.
items.bron: South African History Online, 'First cable connection between SA and Europe launched' (31 July 1879, via Aden, laid under Charles Tilston Bright); Stellenbosch University IT blog (first submarine cable system in South Africa, 1879, Durban–Zanzibar–Aden). Mapping checked: the comparison maps only the route (under the sea), and that holds. It does not map the signal; telegraph cables carried electric current through copper, not light. As worded the sentence does not claim they carried light, so the mapping is sound, but the writer should not widen the comparison to 'net soos die telegraaf ... as lig'.

items.bewering: Vroeër het briewe onder 'n gemerkte klip gewag totdat 'n skip hulle oor die see neem. Nou loop die nuus dadelik deur 'n kabel onder dieselfde see.
items.bron: Dictionary of South African English, 'post office stone'; SAHRIS (SA Heritage Resources Agency) record of the Iziko postal stone naming the ships Banda, Wassenaer and Egmont; Wikipedia, 'Postage stamps and postal history of the Cape of Good Hope' (letters left under inscribed stones at Table Bay from about 1615/1619 for passing ships). 'Dieselfde see': Table Bay is on the Atlantic, and the Atlantic-coast cables SAT-3/WASC, SAFE and Equiano land at Melkbosstrand, WACS and 2Africa at Yzerfontein, ACE and 2Africa at Duynefontein, all near Cape Town (Submarine Networks, South Africa stations; ITWeb). Mapping of the contrast holds: letters waited weeks or months for a ship; data crosses in a fraction of a second, which is 'dadelik' at this level.

items.bewering: Eers het wetenskaplikes begin om rekenaars met mekaar te verbind.
items.bron: Internet Society, 'Brief History of the Internet'; ARPANET 1969, first nodes at UCLA and SRI connected by research teams under Leonard Kleinrock; built to serve researchers and later joined to the National Science Foundation's NSFNET (1986) for academic research (Meiji University seminar notes). The ordering word 'eers' is correct: research networks came before public use.

items.bewering: Later is die internet vir almal oopgemaak, en het dit baie makliker geword om te gebruik. Toe kon gewone mense ook op die internet kom.
items.bron: NSFNET's ban on commercial traffic lifted in the early 1990s and NSFNET retired in 1995 as connections moved to commercial providers (UCSD 'History of the Internet'; Internet Society history); CERN timeline: World Wide Web software put in the public domain on 30 April 1993; NCSA Mosaic (1993) an easy-to-use graphical browser for non-specialists (CERN 'Web History'). Both halves of the sentence happened in the same years; the sentence joins them with 'en' and claims no cause, which is accurate.

items.bewering: E-pos is pos wat elektronies loop in plaas van in 'n possak. 'n Brief het dae geneem, maar 'n e-pos is gou daar.
items.bron: IONOS Digital Guide, 'What happens when you send an e-mail?' and Namecheap, 'How does email work?' (sent electronically via SMTP between mail servers, usually delivered within seconds or minutes). The sentence order does not imply that e-mail came after the internet was opened to the public, so the fact that e-mail is older (ARPANET, early 1970s) does not contradict it.

items.bewering: 'n Soekmasjien help jou om die bladsy te vind wat jou vraag beantwoord.
items.bron: Standard description of a web search engine as a program that finds and lists pages matching a query (Cornell DigLib ch. 2). 'Help jou ... vind' is appropriately modest: it does not promise that the first page is correct.

items.bewering: Nou kan jy enige tyd na inligting soek, waar jy ook al is.
items.bron: DataReportal, 'Digital 2026: South Africa' (79.6% of South Africans online at the end of 2025, so about one in five is not); Econdash/ITU series (78.4% in 2024); ICASA State of the ICT Sector 2026, as reported by Ecofin (rural 4G coverage only 89% in the Northern Cape and 93% in the Eastern Cape); Parliamentary reply citing ICASA 2025 (home broadband about 1% in rural areas). 'Waar jy ook al is' is a universal claim, and it is false: searching needs a device and a connection, and there are places in South Africa, and many more at sea or in remote areas, with neither. A South African Grade 4 learner is exactly the reader most likely to know this from experience.
items.regstelling: Narrow the quantifier and keep the general half: the internet lets you look for information at any time, on many more places than before, as long as you have a phone or computer with a connection to the internet. Do not claim it works everywhere, and do not swap it for a sentence saying it does not work in some places; the point of the item is what the internet changed.

items.bewering: Leerders kan inligting oor 'n onderwerp kry sonder om te reis. Kennis waarna mense vroeër soms dae lank gesoek het, is nou vinnig te kry.
items.bron: Follows from the internet and search-engine definitions above (Internet Society history; Cornell DigLib ch. 2 on the web as a networked information system). Both are worded with 'kan' or 'soms', so they claim no universal.

items.bewering: Selfs 'n klein besigheid kan nou makliker en goedkoper in ander lande koop en verkoop.
items.bron: WTO Business Focus Group 1, 'MSMEs and e-commerce' preliminary report (2016, via tralac): small firms on online platforms are about five times as likely to export; Brookings, 'Supporting the internet as a platform for international trade'. 'Makliker en goedkoper' is comparative, not 'easy and cheap', which matches the WTO/WEF finding that barriers remain.

items.bewering: Nuwe soorte werk het ontstaan wat vroeër nie bestaan het nie. Nou kan baie mense mekaar in een gesprek tegelyk sien en hoor.
items.bron: Web-dependent jobs (web developer, online-shop and social-media roles) date from the 1990s and later, once the web was public (CERN 'Web History'); multi-person video calls over the internet are standard (TCP/IP application layer, Cornell DigLib ch. 2). Neither has a date or quantity that could be wrong.

items.bewering: rekenaar: 'n Masjien wat opdragte volg en inligting stoor, bewerk en wys.
items.bron: Standard computer definition: a device that carries out a program of instructions to store, process and output data (Britannica Dictionary 'handheld' and 'computer' entries; Columbia Computing History on programs as instructions). Simple and not false.

items.bewering: internet: Die wêreldwye netwerk van netwerke wat met dieselfde reëls inligting tussen rekenaars stuur.
items.bron: 1987 TCP/IP primer (funet archive): the internet as a collection of networks connected to each other; Techniques de l'Ingénieur, 'TCP/IP architecture' (networks made to work together by a common protocol, IP). 'Dieselfde reëls' is a correct plain rendering of shared protocols. The study block says 'netwerk van rekenaars' and the glossary 'netwerk van netwerke'; both are true, and a network of networks is still a network of computers.

items.bewering: netwerk: 'n Groep masjiene wat gekoppel is om inligting met mekaar te deel.
items.bron: RIT CS networking notes; Cornell DigLib ch. 2 (computers linked to exchange data).

items.bewering: kabel: 'n Bondel drade of dun glasdrade met 'n sterk laag om hulle.
items.bron: TeleGeography Submarine Cable FAQ (glass fibres about as thin as a hair, wrapped in protective plastic layers and sometimes steel wire, with extra armour near shore); UN World Ocean Assessment ch. 19 on cable armour. Holds for electric cables (insulated wires in a sheath) as well.

items.bewering: e-pos: 'n Boodskap wat oor die internet na iemand se e-posadres gaan en daar wag totdat hy dit lees.
items.bron: Namecheap, 'How does email work?' and Intradyn, 'How does the email system work?' (the recipient's mail server keeps the message in the mailbox until the recipient retrieves it via POP3 or IMAP). The mailbox belonging to the address is where it waits, so the definition is accurate.

items.bewering: soekmasjien: 'n Program wat vir jou bladsye oor 'n onderwerp opspoor.
items.bron: Standard definition of a web search engine as a software system that finds web pages matching a query (Cornell DigLib ch. 2).

items.bewering: laboratorium: 'n Plek waar wetenskaplikes toetse doen en dinge ondersoek.
items.bron: Standard dictionary sense of a laboratory as a room or building for scientific experiments and research (Britannica Dictionary). Not wrong at Grade 4, though school and hospital laboratories are also staffed by technicians; the definition does not say 'only'.

opsomming: Every historical and technical claim holds, including both comparisons (telegraph cables and the Cape post-office stones) and the 'first computers' superlative; the one fault is the list item saying you can search for information 'waar jy ook al is', which is false as a universal, because about one South African in five is not online and rural coverage has gaps, so the writer should narrow it to 'when you have a device with a connection' without turning it into a sentence about where the internet does not work.
